reasoning: South Dakota’s current Senate race is the relevant contest, since there is no presidential race in the state this cycle. The best available recent polling/news points to a Republican lead in the mid-20s: a late-May PPP survey had Mike Rounds ahead by 24 points, while later reporting confirms the Democratic nominee dropped out and the race shifted to Rounds vs. independent Brian Bengs, with no newer state-specific general-election poll in the last 45 days in the provided results. The statewide Cook PVI for South Dakota is R+13.

sources.name: Pollsmax South Dakota Senate polls
sources.details: An aggregate polling page for the 2026 South Dakota Senate race shows Rounds leading at 54.9% to 30.7%, for a R+24.1 average margin based on two polls.

sources.name: Public Policy Polling (as cited by Pollsmax)
sources.details: A Public Policy Polling survey included in the aggregate showed Mike Rounds ahead in the South Dakota Senate matchup; the aggregate page reports this as part of the current race average.

sources.name: NBC News
sources.details: News coverage reported that Democratic nominee Julian Beaudion dropped out of the South Dakota Senate race, leaving Republican incumbent Mike Rounds facing independent Brian Bengs.

sources.name: The New York Times
sources.details: The New York Times also reported Beaudion’s withdrawal and that the race is now Rounds versus independent Brian Bengs.
